name: MLX-LM KV cache quantization disables batching: concurrency vs memory tradeoff
symptom: Enabling KV cache quantization (4-bit or 8-bit) in MLX-LM disables batching entirely, reducing the server to single-request inference. This is a hard tradeoff: save memory or serve concurrent users, not both.
root_cause: MLX-LM's KV cache quantization and batching are separate code paths that are mutually exclusive. The quantized KV cache path does not support the batched decode path. This is a design choice, not a bug, but it is not obvious from the documentation.
workaround: If you need batching, do not enable KV cache quantization. If you need KV cache quantization (for long context or large models), accept single-request inference. For multi-user serving on Apple Silicon, use vLLM-Metal instead of MLX-LM.
notes: This is a critical gotcha for anyone using MLX-LM for serving. The --kv-bits flag (4 or 8) enables KV cache quantization but disables batching. The server will serve one request at a time. For single-user local inference, this is fine. For multi-user serving, use vLLM-Metal which supports both KV cache quantization and continuous batching.
